title: Buffered fully persistent search trees
formal: For every fixed \(0<\varepsilon<1\), can deterministic fully persistent comparison search trees in external memory support amortized update cost \(O(B^{\varepsilon-1}L_v)\), amortized successor queries \(O(L_v)\), sorted range reporting \(O(L_v+K/B)\), and cloning an arbitrary historical version in \(O(1)\) I/Os, with linear total space? Here \(L_v=1+\log_B(2+N_v)\), \(N_v\) is the size of the accessed version and \(K\) is the output size.
definitions: The I/O model has block size \(B\ge2\), internal memory \(M\ge2B\) and unlimited external memory; only transfers of blocks between them are charged. Keys and version handles occupy constant space, and keys support comparisons only. Begin with an empty version. A branch may be extended by inserting or deleting a key, preserving every preceding version; cloning an arbitrary version creates a new independently extendible branch with the same set. All historical versions remain queryable. Search returns the least key at least the supplied key, or an empty marker; Range returns keys in a closed supplied interval. Require correctness for every online sequence. For \(U\) updates and \(C\) clones, linear total space means \(O(1+(U+C)/B)\) external blocks, including version metadata. All bounds may depend on the fixed \(\varepsilon\), but not on sizes, block parameters or the operation sequence. Amortized bounds must hold jointly over every finite history; buffering cannot postpone a query answer past its operation.
why: Efficient historical branching together with buffered writes would combine two major capabilities of storage indexes without sacrificing their I/O savings.

context_blocks.text: The 2025 result obtains the buffered bounds with partial persistence: every historical version can be queried, but only the newest can be extended.

The paper separately describes constant-I/O cloning for unbuffered fully persistent trees and leaves efficient cloning with buffered full persistence open. This card fixes the simultaneous target rather than treating persistence and buffering separately.

progress.text: Optimal partial persistence is achieved; the conclusion leaves buffered full persistence with efficient cloning open.

answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the same inputs, computation model, space allowance, quantifiers and cost guarantees. A result for a restricted input family or a different model does not decide the full target.
status_note: Open in the cited dated sources. The bounded source and subsequent-result review on 13 September 2026 found no verified resolution of this target; this is not exhaustive certification of current openness.

notes: The source asks for efficient cloning without a single numerical combined theorem. This card makes the desired combination explicit using its buffered partial-persistence bounds, constant-I/O cloning benchmark and linear-history-space convention; it is a stated editorial sharpening, not a verbatim theorem conjectured in the paper.

importance.reason: Efficient historical branching together with buffered writes would combine two major capabilities of storage indexes without sacrificing their I/O savings.

category_assignment.reason: Ordered external-memory indexing, buffering and version branching are general data-structure operations.

sentences: A search tree keeps all previous versions of its ordered set.
A user may start a new branch from any past version.
Buffered updates save external-memory transfers by processing writes together.
The goal combines these savings with fast historical queries and constant-I/O cloning.
The latest cited result supplies this update efficiency only for partial persistence.
